newsitem.title: USA: Ashland says refining margins boost qtr.
newsitem.headline: Ashland says refining margins boost qtr.

text.p: Ashland Inc said that lower crude oil prices improved refining margins from $4.80 per barrel to $5.98 per barrel, helping the company post its best ever quarterly performance for the third quarter of its financial year. Ashland's fiscal year ends September 30.
The company said in a statement with earnings that net income was $126 million, or $1.66 per share, compared with $80 million, $1.16 a share, a year ago.
The company also said that per barrel expenses were lower, despite lower throughputs and it is on target to limit capital spending on refining to $100 million for the full year.
Refining throughput fell to 367,800 barrels per day from 376,000 in the year ago quarter and refining and marketing cash flow rose to $200 million from $164 million a year ago.
Refining and marketing sales for the quarter fell to $1.67 billion from $1.71 billion and operating income at the division, which is to become part of a joint venture with USX-Marathon Group.
Operating income at the division was $96 million, up from $53 million.
Overall, analysts had been looking for EPS of $1.33.
Ashland chief executive Paul Chellgren said that negotiation of a definitive agreement on the downsteam merger were underway and that a deal will be signed the end of this year.
He said that the impact of the sale of its upstream Blazer Energy unit, its coal merger and lower debt would be seen in Ashland's fourth quarter, which ends in September.
"We completed the sale with remarkable speed on July 1 for $566 million, which will result in a significant gain in the September quarter," Chellgren said of Blazer.
Ashland Chemical had revenues of $1.07 billion, up from $958 million in the quarter and operating income at the division was $51 million compared with $47 million.
Sales at its Valvoline division fell to $297 million from $350 million and operating income was $30 million, down from $37 million.
"Due to the extremely cool spring, sales volumes of R-12 automotive refrigerant declined, which led to lower overall results for the quarter," Chellgren said.
Ashland's highway construction division had sales of $347 million compared with $356 million a year ago and operating income of $29 million, the same as a year ago.
Chellgren said the unit had a record order backlog of $701 million.
The company also said it was working to resolve a dispute with Nigeria over production sharing agreements, where it produces 20,000 barrels of oil per day.
